Getting started with ztR

ztR.Rmd

ztR (Zircon–Tourmaline–Rutile) is a small toolbox for mineral chemistry and zircon geochronology that works the tidy way: a data frame goes in, the same data frame comes out with new columns. It wraps the heavy lifting of packages such as IsoplotR so you do not have to deal with their own data classes.

library(ztR)
library(tidyverse)

What is in the package

Topic Functions Article
Mineral formulae (APFU) chemical_formula() vignette("mineral-formula")
Zircon trace elements normalize(), ratio_calculator(), anomaly() vignette("zircon-geochemistry")
Thermometry and oxybarometry zircon_ti_t(), zircon_ti_p(), FMQ() vignette("zircon-geochemistry")
Source-rock classification classify_rock_long(), classify_rock_short(), classify_rock_long_no_ce() vignette("zircon-geochemistry")
Parent-rock composition WR_calculator(), WR_crustal_thickness(), crustal_thickness() vignette("zircon-geochemistry")
U-Pb ages use_isoplotr() vignette("u-pb-geochronology")
Concordia diagrams geom_concordia(), geom_concordia_line() vignette("u-pb-geochronology")

Conventions

ztR expects lower-case column names made of the element symbol and the mass of the measured isotope, and uncertainties in a column with the same name plus the suffix _2s:

Quantity Column Uncertainty
La (ppm) la139 la139_2s
U (ppm) approx_u approx_u_2s
207Pb/235U pb207_u235 pb207_u235_2s
206Pb/238U pb206_u238 pb206_u238_2s
207Pb/206Pb pb207_pb206 pb207_pb206_2s
Wetherill error correlation rho_206pb_238u_v_207pb_235u —
Tera-Wasserburg error correlation rho_207pb_206pb_v_238u_206pb —
  • Concentrations are in ppm.
  • Uncertainties are 2-sigma absolute.
  • Ages are in Ma.
  • Chondrite-normalized values get the suffix _N; whole-rock estimates the suffix _WR.

Reading an Iolite export

The package ships a table of reference zircons (91500, Plešovice, FC-1 and PCIGR-1) exported from Iolite. Iolite names columns like la139_ppm_mean and la139_ppm_2se_int; one rename_with() brings them to the ztR convention:

zircons <- read_csv(system.file("extdata", "stds_zircon.csv", package = "ztR"),
                    show_col_types = FALSE, name_repair = "unique_quiet") %>%
  rename_with(~ .x %>%
                str_replace_all("_mean|_ppm", "") %>%
                str_replace_all("_2se_int", "_2s")) %>%
  mutate(sample = recode(sample, "91500-G" = "91500", "FC1" = "FC-1"))

zircons %>% count(sample)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 2
#>   sample     n
#>   <chr>  <int>
#> 1 91500   1789
#> 2 FC-1     756
#> 3 PCIGR1    42
#> 4 PL       512

The same object is used in the other articles.

A first pipeline

Every function adds columns, so they chain:

zircons %>%
  filter(sample == "PL") %>%
  slice(1:5) %>%
  normalize(element_vector = c(la139:lu175)) %>%
  mutate(eu_eu = anomaly(eu153_N, sm147_N, gd157_N),
         t_ti  = zircon_ti_t(ti_ppm = ti49)) %>%
  select(sample, eu_eu, t_ti)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 3
#>   sample eu_eu  t_ti
#>   <chr>  <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 PL     0.403  985.
#> 2 PL     0.397 1004.
#> 3 PL     0.357 1013.
#> 4 PL     0.416  987.
#> 5 PL     0.395  993.

Backwards compatibility

Version 0.0.0.9001 fixed several bugs (see NEWS.md). Old code keeps running:

  • ratio_calculator() and use_isoplotr() return their old columns by default (legacy = TRUE) and warn once per session about what those columns really contain;
  • add_concordia_line() still exists, with its original (transposed) axes; geom_concordia_line() is the new version.
